When checking sitemap membership, grep the filename with -i together with the comment markers "<!--|-->" in one call, because an entry inside an XML comment matches the filename grep but is not indexed; sitemap.xml already has commented blocks (lines 55-56, 206-207, 226).

In the first turn, grep the page for `<script|</script>` with -n in the same batch as the ld+json grep, so the JSON-LD block's end line is known and the parse check is one Read with exact offset and limit; this page's block ran lines 86-237 and cost a second turn to find the end.

When a page's og:title or og:description matches its own JSON-LD (Article headline or description), treat that as no evidence of correctness; compare the OG strings literally against PAGE_META ogTitle and ogDesc and report any difference.

When a page carries a "SEO Patch:" marker comment, check the tag that follows it before judging the head; seo-patch.js line 232 skips any file containing "SEO Patch: Canonical", so a marker with no canonical after it is a latent skip on re-run, not a missing canonical when a canonical exists elsewhe
In the first grep batch, add `(?i)</?script` on the target page next to the ld+json grep, so the JSON-LD start and end lines are known and the single Read of that block needs no extra lookup turn.

When grepping the sitemap for a filename, also grep `<!--|-->` -n in the same batch, so a hit inside a comment block is not counted as indexed (sitemap.xml has commented-out entries, e.g. lines 55-56 and 206-207).

When a page is missing from sitemap.xml, grep the sitemap case-insensitively for "<!--" with line numbers before reporting not-in-sitemap, because its comment blocks record deliberate omissions and additions; a page with no comment naming it, no noindex and a self-referencing canonical is the defect
In the first turn, add a case-insensitive `</script>` grep to the head-tag grep, so the JSON-LD Read gets its offset and limit in one turn instead of needing a second round.

In the first grep batch, add `<!--|-->` to the sitemap.xml and page greps. A sitemap entry inside a comment block is not indexed, and a head tag inside a comment is not present, and neither shows up in a plain filename or tag grep.

For a page audit, put `<!--|-->` and `</script>` in the first grep batch with the tag greps (-n), so the JSON-LD span and any commented-out tags are known before one head-window Read; a tag inside a `<!-- -->` span is not live.

When grepping sitemap.xml for a filename, use the exact filename with no -C context (output_mode content or files_with_matches); a stem pattern with -C 2 hit the 250-line output cap and cut off the tail, forcing a re-grep.

Once a first-turn grep gives the line of an `application/ld+json` opener, Read from that line with a limit near 50 directly; do not grep for `</script>` to find the close, since it matches a dozen script tags per page and costs an extra turn.
Before counting a sitemap `<loc>` as indexed, grep sitemap.xml for `<!--|-->` and confirm the entry's line is outside every comment block, because the sitemap comments mark retired and noindex pages.

Grep a page's filename only in named files (sitemap.xml, seo-patch.js), never repo-wide; a repo-wide grep returns .claude/arena/runs.jsonl as one huge omitted line, and the CLAUDE.md and agent-file hits add nothing to the audit.

Find the JSON-LD block's closing line with a Grep for `</script>` using -n and head_limit 0, then Read that span in one call; a low head_limit cut off the hits before line 224, which cost an extra grep and three Reads here.
To check that a page's JSON-LD parses, Read the block from its `ld+json` line (about 50 lines) rather than grepping `</script>`, which matches every inline script on the page.

In the first grep batch, include </script> (-n -o) alongside ld\+json, then Read the JSON-LD span starting at the opener line itself (for index.html, offset 118, not 117, because line 117 is the 5K minified CSS line), with limit = closer − opener + 1, so the JSON check takes one read and no extra tu

For the sitemap check, also grep sitemap.xml for "<!--|-->" and confirm the page's <loc> line falls outside every comment block, because sitemap.xml wraps entries in multi-line comments (for example lines 55-56 and 206-207), so a filename hit can sit inside a comment.

When a tag grep prints "[Omitted long matching line]", the tag sits on a one-line script (the JSON-LD blocks on this template do). Run a bounded `-o -n` grep such as `<script[^>]{0,200}ld\+json` to get its line number, then Read that single line with offset and limit 1 instead of the surrounding blo

In the first grep batch, also grep seo-patch.js for the bare slug 'junk-removal' case-insensitive next to the '.html' filename, and grep the page for '</script>' alongside 'ld+json', so PAGE_META absence and the JSON-LD block bounds come back in one batch instead of a second round trip.

Put a grep for `</script>` (or `ld\+json|</script>`) in the same first batch as the tag greps, so the ld+json Read is one exact offset/limit range, and grep the sitemap for the slug together with `<!--|-->` in that batch so a commented-out `<loc>` is caught without a second pass.

When PAGE_META has an entry, grep seo-patch.js once for `ogDesc`: lines 125 and 133 write og:description and twitter:description from the same field, so a description drift is one og-mismatch finding that cites both tags, not two findings.
To check JSON-LD, grep "ld\+json|</script>" in the same turn as the tag greps to get the block's exact start and end lines, then Read only that range.

When grepping the page for the JSON-LD block, put `</script>` in the same pattern as `ld+json` so the block's start and end lines return together, then read that range once with offset and limit; the agent file's ld+json-only grep forces an extra round trip to find the closing tag.

After a sitemap.xml filename hit, run one case-insensitive grep for '<!--|-->' with -n and no context to confirm the <url> entry is not inside an XML comment. The sitemap carries comment blocks that document omissions, and a commented-out entry still matches a filename grep.

When grepping sitemap.xml for a filename, add -C 2 so a <loc> sitting inside an XML comment block is visible, because the file comments out omissions and a bare filename grep cannot tell live entries from commented ones.

To find where a page's ld+json block closes, grep the page for ^</script> anchored at line start, not bare </script>. The bare pattern returns every inline script closer (about 20 on these pages) and adds reads that prove nothing.

Before calling a head tag or sitemap entry present, grep '<!--|-->' in the page and in sitemap.xml in the same turn as the tag greps, because a commented-out tag still matches a bare-token grep, and sitemap.xml wraps city and blog entries in multi-line comments (for example lines 55-56 and 206-207).

For a page whose robots meta is noindex, one case-insensitive Grep with the alternation `canonical|og:|twitter:|ld\+json|robots|refresh` on the page covers every head check, and the page's tags can be checked in that one call without a separate Read of the head.

In the first grep batch, add </script> and <!--|--> to the page's tag grep. That returns the JSON-LD block's end line and shows any head tag sitting inside an HTML comment in the same pass, so no second grep round is needed.

After grepping sitemap.xml for the filename, also grep it for `<!--|-->`. Entries can sit inside comment blocks (sitemap.xml lines 55-56 and 206-207 document intentional omissions), and a filename grep cannot distinguish a live entry from a commented one.

For not-in-sitemap, grep sitemap.xml for the filename and for `<!--|-->` in the same call. sitemap.xml has multi-line comments (lines 55-56 and 206-207), and a <loc> inside one is not indexed even though the filename matches.

For JSON-LD parse checks, Grep `ld\+json|</script>` with -n in one call, then Read from the opening script line through the first closing `</script>` in a single range; the 64-line block here took two 40-line reads because the closing tag was not located first.

In the first turn, grep `</script>` with -n alongside the ld+json grep; the JSON-LD block closes at the first `</script>` after its `application/ld+json` opener, so the JSON check takes one Read from opener to close and no head Read.

When checking sitemap.xml membership, grep `<!--|-->` in sitemap.xml alongside the filename, because the file wraps entries in comment blocks (for example lines 55-56 and 206-207), and a `<loc>` hit inside one is not live.
Before reporting PAGE_META absent, grep the filename stem without ".html" case-insensitively in seo-patch.js, since a key written without the extension is missed by the full-filename grep.

In the first batch, grep the page for `ld\+json|</script>` alongside the tag greps and grep `<!--|-->` too, so the JSON-LD block's end line and any comment-wrapped tags are known before the Read; the head check then takes two turns instead of three.
On the first turn, grep `</script>|<script` on the page alongside the tag grep to get the ld+json block bounds, so the JSON-LD can be read with a single offset/limit Read in the second turn.
When a sitemap.xml grep hits a filename, also grep `<!--|-->` in the same turn and confirm the hit sits outside any comment block, since a loc inside an open comment is not indexed.
Put `</script>` in the first page grep alongside `ld\+json`, so the JSON-LD Read range (offset and limit) is known in the first batch instead of costing a second turn.

For a page absent from PAGE_META, one grep of seo-patch.js for `PAGE_META\s*\[` returns the unmapped-page warning lines (about 238-248) that state what the script will skip for that page, so cite those lines for page_meta-gap instead of reading the config block.

When checking a sitemap entry, grep sitemap.xml for `<!--|-->` with -n in the same turn as the filename grep. A `<loc>` line that falls between an opening `<!--` and its closing `-->` is commented out and not indexed, and a filename grep alone cannot show that.

In the first batch, grep the page for `ld\+json|</script>` together with the head-tag grep, so the JSON-LD block's closing line is known and one Read covers it; for seo-patch.js, grep `\.html'` once to list every PAGE_META key and confirm absence without a second grep.

For blog/ pages, seo-patch.js scans only the repo root (the `fs.readdirSync(dir)` line near the end, about line 387), so a blog page's absence from PAGE_META is structural. Cite that line in any page_meta-gap finding at low confidence instead of searching PAGE_META further.

For a blog/ page, a grep of seo-patch.js for its quoted key returning nothing means no PAGE_META entry, so report page_meta-gap at low confidence without searching further; one grep of `^  '[^']+':` lists all PAGE_META keys in a single call to confirm coverage.

For a short head (about 15 lines or fewer), one Read with offset 0 and limit 15 can replace the separate tag greps. It shows the canonical, refresh, robots meta and the absence of OG, twitter and ld+json by inspection in a single call, which is cheaper than two grep turns plus a Read.

In the first page grep, add `<script` and `</script>` to the tag pattern so both ld+json block line ranges are known in turn one; then Read those ranges in the same turn as the PAGE_META bare-slug grep and the sitemap grep, which keeps the run to two main turns.

On a page with several ld+json blocks, grep `</script>|ld\+json` with -n once to get every block's line span, then Read the first-to-last span in one call (usually under 100 lines) instead of one Read per block.

Before counting a sitemap hit as indexed, grep the filename with -B 2 -A 2 to confirm it is not inside a multi-line XML comment (sitemap.xml has them at about lines 55, 118-143 and 206); do not grep the bare `<url>` tag, which returns the whole file.
A page under `.claude/arena/canaries/` is not served and is not a root page, so a sitemap miss there is expected. Still grep sitemap.xml, but log the miss under EXCLUDED, not as not-in-sitemap.

For an item under .claude/arena/canaries/, a sitemap miss and a PAGE_META miss are expected, because the fixture is not a served site page and seo-patch.js only touches root HTML. List both under EXCLUDED with that reason, and still run all five tag checks on the file.

On a page whose filename names no city, set PAGE-CITY to none and test locality with one grep for "in [A-Z][a-z ]+, S\.?C|serving|local [A-Z][a-z]+ provider" plus the areaServed block; "Florence, SC" in body copy on such pages is the business's home, so it is not a wrong-city finding.

For absolute-URL checks, grep with -o and the pattern https?://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+; a combined alternation (http://|www\.|city names) hit head_limit at line 474 and hid the body's later matches, which cost a second grep.

When a page's JSON-LD areaServed or footer names a city other than its own, grep that exact entry across the series' sibling pages with files_with_matches before weighing it; an entry shared by every sibling guide is template, not a locality claim.

For the domain check, grep `https?://[a-z0-9.-]+` with -o and -n, and write `<` literally in patterns, because an `<` inside a character class silently truncates every match (this cost a re-run here); treat the template-wide form backend `florence-crm-api.cball8475.workers.dev` as content, not a

In placeholder-token greps, drop `\}\}` from the pattern: inline `<style>` closing braces match on every page (here lines 548, 588, 589) and cost a second call. Use `\{\{[A-Za-z_ ]+\}\}` or `%[A-Z_]{3,}%` instead.

For the phone inventory, one grep with -o and -n over tel:[^"]* plus the (ddd) ddd-dddd pattern lists every tel: target and displayed number with line numbers in about 20 lines; add -C context only to the lines that look wrong.

For city-claim checks, grep with -o -n and a character-class pattern that skips the brand, e.g. Florence([,.;:)!?]|\s[^S]|\sS[^C]|\sSC[^ ]|\sSC\s[^S]). Treat absolute https://florencescservices.com/... URLs as internal, not external: strip the origin and test the repo-root path, since the "ignore https" rule is meant for third-party hosts only.
